newsitem.title: USA: Apple, Sun link Internet technology.
newsitem.headline: Apple, Sun link Internet technology.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. and Sun Microsystems Inc. will on Wednesday showcase technical collaboration for their Internet technologies, industry sources said Tuesday.

The joint development work is broadly aimed at combining Apple's multimedia capabilities and position in the graphics and publishing worlds with the Java programming technology created by Sun Microsystems, the sources said.
The companies want to promote the ability of these technologies to work across a variety of computers, and in particular, to make it easier to use Apple and Sun computers together, the sources said.

The companies said Apple's new Chief Technology Officer, Ellen Hancock, Chief Administrative Officer George Scalese and Sun Microsystmes Chief Technology Officer Eric Schmidt will hold a news conference in Atlanta on Wednesday to discuss the joint Internet and multimedia technology efforts.
Spokeswomen for the two companies declined to elaborate on the announcements.
Sources familiar with details of the collaboration to be unveiled at the Networld+Interop trade show said they revolved around several key technological areas.

This includes making it possible for Apple's QuickTime computer motion picture technology to run within Java media, the sources said. They said Sun's Sunsoft unit also will show advances improving links between Sun Microsystem's network servers, which can work as hubs in the World Wide Web, and Apple's Macintosh desktop computers.
Finally, the companies will discuss advances in network management through their collaboration.
